subject: CortexA - Dedicated Footprint & Throughput Workback
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivers <alex.rivers@cortexa.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: CortexA - Dedicated Footprint & Throughput Workback

Alex — thanks for the traffic profile you dropped in yesterday (attached csv). Quick pass below with an initial sizing sketch and next steps so we can lock a slab and procurement window. High-level assumptions:
- Model: Redwood-7B-v2 (q4) serving generation flows (mix of chat + single-turn completion).
- Peak traffic (provided): 3,500 tokens/sec for peak 90th minute; median steady 1,200 tokens/sec.
- Avg output+prompt length (CortexA profile): 64 tokens. Burst patterns: 6x short bursts during business hours.

Initial throughput math:
- Measured (our benchmark) for Redwood-7B-v2 (q4) on A100-40GB: ~550 tokens/sec/GPU (steady gen, batch=1, seq=64).
- Contended/streaming penalty: -10% when many concurrent streams (p95-sensitive). Effective conservative throughput ~= 500 tokens/sec/GPU.
- Baseline GPUs needed for peak = ceil(3500 / 500) = 7 GPUs.
- Recommended headroom: 30% for traffic variance + KV cache cold starts = 7 * 1.3 -> ~9.1 -> round to 10 GPUs.

Proposal:
- Dedicated slab: 10 x A100-40GB (primary), configured with autoscale reserve (burst pool +2 GPUs) and warm KV cache policy.
- SLO alignment: target customer p95 latency < 200ms on generation paths. With the 10-GPU slab and cache warmups we project p95 ~ 140-160ms under peak.
- Fallback policy: if slab saturates, route non-critical low-priority requests to hosted-compatible lower-cost variant (Redwood-7B-q4-approx) with degraded QoS.

Action items I need from CortexA to finalize quote:
1) Confirm that 3,500 tokens/sec peak is the correct peak minute target (csv shows spikes; confirm which percentile to plan to).
2) Annotate what percent of requests must hit p95 <200ms vs acceptable best-effort.
3) Any firm commit horizon / desired start date for dedicated capacity (we recommend 4-week lead for slab provisioning + onboarding).

Attached: cortexa_token_profile.csv (your traffic), I'll follow up with a formal slab quote and a short runbook.

- Michael Grant
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: CortexA - Dedicated Footprint & Throughput Workback

Michael — thanks, this is helpful. Quick clarifications:
- The 3,500 tokens/sec number is peak for the product search assistant (90th-minute). For contract planning we'd prefer to size to the 95th-minute peak if possible — that number runs ~4,600 tokens/sec per our logs.
- Our SLAs: product-search assistant needs p95 <250ms for interactive users; async batch scoring can be best-effort. Roughly 70% of requests are interactive.
- Preferred start: target go-live 2026-11-01.

Can you re-run the math using 4,600 tokens/sec and call out the slab+commit options? Also we need an approx monthly committed cost to present to finance.

— Alex
Head of Engineering | CortexA
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-23T13:15:00-07:00
Subject: RE: CortexA - Dedicated Footprint & Throughput Workback

Michael / team — did a quick alternative calc for 4,600 tokens/sec (Alex's 95th-minute). Using the same conservative per-GPU effective throughput (500 tps):
- GPUs required = ceil(4600 / 500) = 10 GPUs.
- With 30% headroom -> 10 * 1.3 = 13 -> round to 14 GPUs to stay conservative and reduce risk of SLA breach during multi-burst minutes.

Notes on tuning to reduce slab size:
- KV cache priming for product-search (many repeated prefixes) can recover ~15% effective throughput once warmed; that could reduce sustained need from 14 -> ~12 GPUs.
- Quantized 3-bit variants (q3) could improve token/sec by ~20% in our internal tests, but require a brief quality pass with CortexA samples. That could let us target 10 GPUs with similar p95.
- Batch-size tuning and a small request coalescer for background scoring can shift non-interactive load off the slab during peaks.

I'll draft two configuration options for the quote: (A) conservative 14-GPU slab with guaranteed SLA and 2-GPU burst reserve, (B) optimized 10-GPU slab conditioned on a KV-cache warmup plan + q3 validation.

-- Priyom
Principal SRE, Inference Optimization | Redwood Inference

- Committed monthly cost: $68,000/month
- SLA: 99.9% uptime for slab, p95 generation latency target <200ms (per engineering validation).
- Provisioning lead: 3–4 weeks after PO date.

Option 2 — Optimized (10 x A100-40GB) + feature gating (KV warmers & q3 validation)

- Provisioning lead: 3 weeks.

Add-ons: 24/7 on-call SLA, dedicated onboarding runbook (attached), 1-off warm cache warmup assist engagement (2 engineer-days).

Please confirm preferred option and whether CortexA will accept the validation conditions for Option 2. I'll attach the formal quote (rw_dedicated_quote_Q3.xlsx) and the onboarding runbook.

Regards,
Irene Choi

Thanks — quick operational plan / workback to meet 2026-11-01 go-live if CortexA issues PO by 2026-10-04: 
Week 0 (PO issued): legal & billing kickoff; reserve slab order in procurement queue.
Week 1–2: q3 quant validation (Redwood runs against 500 sample prompts provided by CortexA; quality pass/fail and token/sec delta reported).
Week 2: onboarding runbook handoff; JV cache-warm plan agreed (we provide small harness + sample script).
Week 3: slab provisioning + network setup; pre-warm KV cache with synthetic replay for request shapes.
Week 4: canary traffic (5–10% of traffic) into dedicated slab; latency validation and SLA signoff.
Day 31 (target go-live 2026-11-01): full traffic cutover.

Attachments in this thread: cortexa_token_profile.csv, rw_dedicated_quote_Q3.xlsx, runbook_dedicated_onboarding.md (stubs attached). I pushed a short shared Drive folder with the validation template: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1CortexA-Deck
